base_properties.human_readable: The Homoiousios Settlement: Middle-Formula Communion Discipline (Semi-Arian Reading)

stakeholders.name: constantius_ii_court
stakeholders.situation: Convokes councils, drafts and redrafts the confessional formula through court bishops, and enforces subscription by deposing and banishing bishops who refuse. Gains a church whose public doctrine tracks palace policy and whose episcopate can be reshuffled at will. When a formula stops serving, it replaces it — by 359-360 it has moved past substance-language altogether. Its horizon is the reign; its exit is total, since it authored the machinery and can redirect it.

stakeholders.name: homoiousian_episcopal_bloc
stakeholders.situation: Bishops centered in Asia Minor and Syria (Basil of Ancyra, George of Laodicea, Eustathius of Sebaste) teach that the Son is generated from the Father's own substance and is like him in substance, while insisting the two remain really distinct. They staff the councils that promote this formula, condemn the radicals on one flank, and negotiate with the court on the other. In exchange they keep their sees, their communion, and a decisive voice in the church's public confession. Their position depends on continued court favor and on both flanks staying discredited; they cannot join the Nicene party without discarding their life's work, nor the radicals without betraying their theology.

stakeholders.name: pro_nicene_deposed_bishops
stakeholders.situation: Bishops who hold the Nicene confession and refuse every middle formula as a disguised retreat from it. They lose their sees to subscribers, endure repeated banishment (Athanasius to Trier and the desert, Eusebius of Vercelli and Lucifer to the east, Hilary to Phrygia), and organize from exile — letters, synods, monastic networks. Signing would end the exile; it would also, in their own eyes, end everything they are. Their refusal is the chief obstacle the enforcement campaigns exist to overcome, and eventually the ground of the settlement's defeat.

stakeholders.name: anomoean_theologians
stakeholders.situation: Radical teachers (Aetius, Eudoxius) who hold the Son to be unlike the Father in substance and created from nothing. The middle party condemns and deposes them — Ankyra in 358 — precisely to demonstrate its own orthodoxy. They lose posts and platforms, regroup around the court, and answer each middle formula by pressing a more minimal one.

stakeholders.name: congregations_of_disputed_sees
stakeholders.situation: The baptized of Antioch, Alexandria, Constantinople, and smaller cities receive each successive formula from whichever bishop holds their altar. They lose pastors to deposition cycles, absorb liturgical and doctrinal whiplash, and sometimes riot or barricade churches for an expelled bishop. They cannot leave the church without leaving everything; they also receive whatever stability each settlement buys. Most learn the newest creed by decree.

stakeholders.name: homoean_court_party
stakeholders.situation: Court-aligned bishops (Ursacius, Valens, Acacius) who compete with the middle party for the palace's ear. Every successive compromise further discredits the Nicene term, which serves their program of a minimal, substance-free formula. They contribute to the same councils and enforcement campaigns, collect seats and influence from the process, and abandon each formula as soon as a thinner one becomes available.

stakeholders.name: ecclesiastical_historians
stakeholders.situation: Later analysts working from acta, creeds, letters, and chronicles. They reconstruct who signed what under what pressure, trace the middle party's dissolution into the Nicene settlement, and distinguish conviction from coercion in the subscription lists. They collect nothing and pay nothing; their seat is retrospective.

six_questions.coordination_function: After Nicaea, the church needed a confessional floor wide enough to hold the eastern episcopal majority — which read homoousios as collapsing Father and Son into one acting subject — without surrendering the Son's real divinity to the Arian reading. The homoiousios formula supplied that floor: bishops who rejected both the Nicene term and the Arian denial could share councils, communion, and a common disciplinary front. It solved, for a generation, the collective-action problem of keeping one church out of two irreconcilable communions.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves confessional assent and episcopal office: a bishop who subscribes keeps his see, his altar, and his congregation; a bishop who refuses transfers both to a subscriber and typically goes into exile. Upward, it moves deference — the episcopate's public uniformity flows to the court as proof of a governable church. Downward, it moves doctrinal legitimacy from council to congregation, with each revision resetting what the baptized must treat as settled.
six_questions.absent_voices: The laity of disputed sees had no seat at any council that revised their confession; ascetic and monastic communities — already the church's mobilized conscience — objected from outside the episcopal process; rank-and-file clergy learned each new formula by decree. Western bishops at Ariminum were asked to ratify text agreed elsewhere. The unanimity the councils announced was produced among a subscribed episcopate; the baptized majority absorbed each revision without consent.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: Sees, communions, and court-church relations were arranged around subscription to the middle formula. Overnight removal in, say, 355 forces every bishop back onto the Nicene-or-Arian binary immediately: depositions reverse or multiply, the court loses its instrument of episcopal management, and congregations realign around whichever communion their next bishop chooses. The settlement's disappearance is not a return to a prior equilibrium — the prior equilibrium no longer exists.
six_questions.founding_problem: Express the Son's relation to the Father in a formula that neither collapsed the two into one subject (the eastern reading of homoousios) nor divided the deity (the Arian teaching) — a scriptural, non-materialist middle term that could anchor a stable settlement.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Attested from outside the benefiting parties: Athanasius' De Synodis (359) — written by the arrangement's principal target — analyzed the middle creeds and predicted their dissolution into either Nicaea or bare Arianism; the Constantinopolitan council's reaffirmation of Nicaea in 381 attests the middle project's failure; the Homoean party's abandonment of substance-language altogether attests it independently; modern historiography of the fourth century treats the homoiousian program as concluded by absorption. No party inside the benefiting set disputes the termination.

commentary.narrative_context:
Between the Dedication Council of Antioch (341) and the Council of Constantinople (381), the church's public confession was governed by a middle formula: the Son is generated from the Father's own substance and is like (homoiousios) the Father, while remaining really distinct from him. The formula was a deliberate mediation — rejecting both the Nicene term (read in the east as Sabellian collapse) and the Arian denial (creation from nothing) — and it was held in place by an enforcement economy: councils convoked under imperial authority, sees transferred to subscribers, refusers deposed and banished. This story authors epsilon for the standing arrangement under contest — the homoiousios settlement as it actually operated across 341-381 — assessed by the reading's own lights: from the semi-Arian seat the coercion of both flanks figures as necessary discipline in defense of a peace-making formula, not as plunder, and the authored epsilon reflects that reading-indexed assessment of a genuinely costly arrangement. The claimed type and the metrics are authored independently.

KEY AGENTS (by structural relationship):
- constantius_ii_court: Primary agenda-setter (institutional/arbitrage) — sets and revises the formula, collects ecclesiastical manageability
- homoiousian_episcopal_bloc: Primary beneficiary (organized/constrained) — supplies the formula's content, collects secure tenure for the middle
- pro_nicene_deposed_bishops: Principal payer (organized/identity_locked) — bears deposition and exile for refusal
- anomoean_theologians: Secondary payer (moderate/constrained) — condemned on the opposite flank
- congregations_of_disputed_sees: Diffuse payer with incidental benefit (powerless/trapped)
- homoean_court_party: Rival beneficiary (organized/arbitrage) — rides the enforcement machinery while undermining the formula
- ecclesiastical_historians: Analytical observer (analytical/analytical)
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness 0.56 characterizes the settlement's operative enforcement era (roughly t10-t24 on the series): sees flowed to subscribers, refusal cost deposition and exile, and the court repriced the formula repeatedly. Suppression 0.60 is authored as a raw structural property, unscaled by power or scope: banishment, conciliar deposition, and forced subscription under threat — episodic and regionally uneven rather than totalizing. Theater 0.30 reflects the operative mix: real conciliar negotiation carrying a growing share of performative 'unity restored' promulgation, each successive creed declaring a final settlement the next council would revise. Accessibility_collapse 0.42: understanding the settlement collapses no alternative — the Nicene term, the court's minimal formula, and the radical denial all remained live, costly exits. Resistance 0.58: two-flank resistance, from an identity-locked Nicene network and from condemned radicals, plus recurring congregational unrest. The scalar metrics characterize the constraint as it operated; the measurement series runs on one shared time grid and documents the full arc — rise to the 359 peak (Rimini-Seleucia), decay after Constantius' death, dissolution at the 381 settlement — so the series endpoints describe a terminated arrangement, not the operative constraint the scalars assess. The claimed type is asserted from structure (a genuine mediation function carrying a subscription economy with identifiable payers), not tuned to any computed verdict.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The same settlement computes differently by seat. From the court's chair it is a governance instrument: authored, revisable, abandoned at will — arbitrage exit puts that seat near the beneficiary pole regardless of how much coercion the machinery applies to others. From the exiled Nicene seat the identical structure is uncompensated loss: identity_locked exit converts every demand for signature into a demand for self-dissolution, pushing that seat toward the full-target pole. From the middle bloc's seat it is home: the formula they wrote, policed against both flanks, sheltering their tenure. One structure, three experienced types; the engine derives this divergence from power, exit, and role data rather than from the authored claim.
commentary.directionality_logic: The court holds beneficiary status with arbitrage exit: derivation places it near the beneficiary pole, and effective extraction damps toward subsidy — it pays little and collects manageability. The homoiousian bloc collects tenure and communion (beneficiary) but pays patronage dependence and flank-policing labor (constrained exit), sitting low-mid. The deposed Nicene bishops are declared victims with identity_locked exit: derivation places them near the full-target pole, amplified — trapped or identity-locked targets sit nearer the target end than mobile ones. The anomoeans are victims with constrained exit: high d, somewhat damped by their court access. Congregations carry both roles: they pay disruption and receive stability, landing near symmetric. The homoean party is a beneficiary in role but a rival in fact — it collects from the machinery without maintaining the formula; its derived d sits near the beneficiary pole, which the story accepts. Continental scope raises verification difficulty and scales effective extraction modestly upward for target-side seats; suppression, by contrast, enters the computation unscaled.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem — a stable middle term anchoring one communion — was never solved; the arrangement ended by absorption rather than persisting past its function. Reading the settlement as pure coordination misses the subscription economy and the exiles; reading it as pure extraction misses that its heirs converged into the victor's framework by argument once the Sabellian fear was answered — the Alexandrian accord of 362 and the Cappadocian hypostasis distinction did what four Sirmium creeds could not. The tangled-rope classification holds both truths: genuine mediation function, asymmetric enforcement cost, identifiable payers. On the genealogy interview the founding problem is dead and the world-rearranges verdict applies to the arrangement's living period; the mismatch flag a dead-status/world-rearranges pairing raises should be cross-checked against theater and persistence — here the arrangement did not outlive its function as performance; it terminated. That is resolution by death, not mandatrophy: nothing theatrical remains to administer.
commentary.kernel_context: This constraint instantiates the semi_arian_reading of the homoousios_christology kernel — the fourth-century middle position associated with Basil of Ancyra and his allies, that the Son is generated from the Father's substance and is of like rather than identical substance with him. Sibling readings: the pro_nicene_reading (homoousios as the required confession) and the arian_reading (the Son as created and subordinate, of no substance with the Father). The semi-Arian reading shares the Arian reading's rejection of the Nicene term while sharing the pro-Nicene reading's rejection of creation-language; its historical fate was absorption into the pro-Nicene settlement after 381 rather than independent persistence.

omegas.question: This constraint is one reading (semi_arian_reading) of the homoousios_christology kernel; what would instantiating a sibling reading change structurally?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Compare the compiled sibling stories: the pro_nicene_reading file and the arian_reading file, examining victim sets, enforcement profiles, and seat structures against this file.
omegas.impact: As pro-Nicene, the payer set shifts to homoian and homoiousian holdouts after 381 and enforcement rises (imperial edicts, expulsions of non-subscribing clergy); as Arian, the mediation function disappears entirely and the arrangement reduces to court-managed doctrinal extraction with no coordinating floor.
omegas.description: Committer structure: this story is one of three readings of a single contested kernel; sibling files instantiate the others.

omegas.question: Did the semi-Arian refusal of homoousios track a real danger (collapse of the persons into one subject) or a misreading exploited for political cover?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Textual-historical analysis of pre-Cappadocian homoousios usage against the 362 Alexandrian accord and the Cappadocian ousia/hypostasis distinction, which resolved the ambiguity the middle party feared.
omegas.impact: If the fear was valid, the middle formula's coordination contribution was substantive and its enforcement cost purchased a real service pending clarification; if invalid, the formula was a stalling device whose extraction bought nothing and the arrangement trends toward pure extraction dressed as mediation.
omegas.description: Whether the reading's core doctrinal objection was sound or strategic.

omegas.question: Was the post-381 disappearance of the homoiousios position absorption (voluntary convergence once safeguards were articulated) or suppression (elimination by imperial enforcement)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Trace individual bishop trajectories 362-394: how many subscribed after argumentation of the De Synodis type versus under edict pressure; count sees lost to enforcement versus voluntarily surrendered.
omegas.impact: Absorption supports the tangled-rope reading (the coordination succeeded, then dissolved into the stronger formula); suppression supports a snare-flavored reading (the middle was never viable, merely tolerated while useful).
omegas.description: Mechanism of the reading's historical termination.

omegas.question: How much of the middle formula's enforcement era was driven by the court's genuine doctrinal preference versus its use of whichever formula maximized leverage over the episcopate?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Compare court behavior across formula transitions (341, 351, 357, 359, 361): did enforcement intensity track doctrinal content or episcopal compliance rates?
omegas.impact: If leverage-driven, the court's directionality sits closer to the target-collecting end than its beneficiary role suggests and the arrangement's extraction is primarily court rent-seeking in doctrinal dress; if preference-driven, the court was a genuine if self-interested coordinatee.
omegas.description: Whether the agenda-setting seat's gains reflect conviction or leverage.

network.dual_formulation_note: The colloquial label 'the Arian controversy' (or 'the homoousios question') covers three structurally distinct constraint stories — three readings of one kernel, each with its own epsilon, beneficiary/victim structure, and fate. This file instantiates the semi_arian_reading: the middle-formula settlement, whose epsilon reflects coerced subscription riding a genuine mediation function, and whose historical endpoint is absorption into the pro-Nicene settlement rather than independent persistence. Linked siblings: pro_nicene_reading (the settlement that absorbed it) and arian_reading (the flank it policed). Decomposition follows the epsilon-invariance principle: the three readings carry different enforcement arrangements and different victim sets, so no single story can hold a stable epsilon across them.
